target: Approved Direct line footer on Music gallery root

productSurfaces.reason: Every Song Is a Website is a single static experience: the gallery is the entry route and song-world routes are its core experience, not a separate marketing landing page and app pair. This bounded change restores footer composition on the gallery root only.

ownerEvidence.quote: i like the second version the most ... game for this component sticking in footer with AI and strip ... feedback hover button can be used as needed

library.primary: Existing SaaS Maker project-strip.js and ai-chat-footer.js custom-element footer composition

contract.purpose: Every Song Is a Website gives each song a curated visual world — a shareable URL with embedded video, licensed lyrics, and playful interactions.
contract.purposeSource: SaaS Maker catalog presentation.directory.purposeContract and PRODUCT.md
contract.canonicalPurpose: Every Song Is a Website gives each song a curated visual world — a shareable URL with embedded video, licensed lyrics, and playful interactions.
contract.audience: Anyone who loves music and the web.
contract.job: Enter the gallery, browse a song, and step into its shareable visual world; optionally request product updates or send feedback from the gallery footer.
contract.thesis: Keep the established music-gallery composition and restore the approved compact Direct line beside AI and the project strip, with feedback available as a separate hover control.
contract.system: Keep the existing static gallery typography, theme tokens, artwork, and layout; reuse the hosted project strip and AI footer custom elements without adding a runtime dependency.
contract.signature: The gallery footer composes newsletter, feedback, and project discovery in one inline shared footer while immersive song routes remain unobstructed.
contract.risk: Shared footer content could compete with the song gallery; constrain this patch to the existing gallery root and keep the form compact and inline.
contract.qualityBar: Preserve the curated gallery identity and hierarchy; make the approved footer available inline at the gallery root; keep song-world and 404 routes free of the strip; show newsletter-only wording with unchecked consent; maintain responsive behavior at 390, 768, and 1440 pixels.

productContinuity.reason: Every Song Is a Website is one static experience with a gallery entry and song-world routes; it has no separate landing/app pair.

slopScale.reason: Preserve lane: established rendered direction is retained. Required iteration and final scans are recorded after the first working local render and final review.

checkpoints.findingsReview: Pinned score 18; the five triggered patterns (gradient backgrounds, colored glows, all-caps labels, permanent dark mode, wide body tracking) match the intentional themed music worlds and existing mono metadata. Screenshot review found no generic-pattern defect caused by the patch; no changes made to chase the advisory score.

Same pinned 2026.09 definitions, full preset, score 18 and five intentional theme/layout triggers as iteration. Final 390/768/1440 review confirms inline responsive footer and no new generic-pattern issue.

visualReview.reviewer: Fleet root rendered QA; implementation agent reviewed retained captures

hierarchy.observation: At 390 px the AI, discovery, inline feedback, and newsletter stack in order; wider layouts group AI and project discovery above feedback and newsletter.

typography.observation: The mono/condensed music identity carries through the footer; the long AI heading wraps narrowly at 1440 px but stays legible.

composition.observation: Footer surfaces remain inline and visually quiet; capture follows shared footer content without a fixed overlay.

identity.observation: Dark mono footer and themed song artwork remain coherent with the established Music gallery direction.

interaction.observation: Feedback dialog opens with title focus and dismisses; focus returns to BODY instead of the launcher, recorded as a P2 shared-widget follow-up.

responsive.observation: 390, 768, and 1440 px captures show stacked/narrow and two-column/wide layouts with no horizontal overflow.
